excerpt: The atom-cavity interaction has a dark state |D⟩ = cos θ |a⟩|0⟩ + sin θ |b⟩|1⟩. In the ideal transfer sequence, |φfield(t)⟩|b⟩ → |0⟩(c1|a⟩ + c0|b⟩) ... → |φfield(t + τ)⟩|b⟩, with Ω1(t) and Ω2(t + τ) controlling absorption into memory and later emission back to the field.
overview: The dark-state construction is the clearest concrete mechanism for reversible light-matter conversion in the source. It explains how a photon can be absorbed into a long-lived atomic superposition and re-emitted later while avoiding population of the lossy excited state in the ideal adiabatic limit.
title: Dark-State Memory Mapping
